findings.evidence: SOURCE 1 shows current page as "WeirdML v3" and lists "Previous versions: WeirdML v2"; the row claims version "2" with version_status "published", implying the maintainer publishes identifier "2", but the published identifier is v3.
findings.repair: Set version to "3" and adjust version_guard accordingly (or, if intentionally retaining v2, mark status "retained" and set superseded_by to the successor registry id).

findings.evidence: SOURCE 1 defines the official score as "80% normalized area under its line on a logarithmic token axis, plus 20% of its final value" over "11 tasks"; the row states "Average Max Accuracy ... averaged over all 17 tasks", a different metric and task count.
findings.repair: Replace the metric with the v3 scoring rule and correct the task count to 11 (matching the protocol's configuration count).

findings.evidence: SOURCE 1 presents v3 as the active version and lists "WeirdML v2" under "Previous versions"; for a row identifying as v2, v3 is the named successor and v2 is no longer reported, so status "active" and superseded_by null contradict the protocol.
findings.repair: If the row is v2, set status to "retained" and superseded_by to the successor registry id (e.g., weirdml::3); if the row is meant to be v3, correct the version and retain active/null.

findings.evidence: SOURCE 1 describes v3 as "11 complex hand-made tasks" to "explore and understand unfamiliar data, develop machine learning and data analysis pipelines" with "limited data, unspecified goals and/or very limited feedback"; the row description says "write, run, and iteratively improve PyTorch code under fixed compute and time limits," which does not match the v3 protocol text.
findings.repair: Align the description with the v3 protocol wording, or clarify the version it describes.

uncertainties: Cannot recompute hashes or execute transport/qualification checks; owner performs those separately.
Successor registry id for v3 is inferred as weirdml::3; exact id depends on registry conventions.
The row may have been intended as a v2 snapshot, but under the current v3 protocol its version, metric, and lifecycle fields would still be mismatched.
